NO CAUSAL-INTERVENTIONAL FABRIC EXTRACTABLE FROM THE PROVIDED DATA SOURCE

Reason in detail:
1. The “paper” supplied consists solely of an 86-item bibliography.  
2. There is no narrative, argumentation, empirical description, theoretical development, or intervention proposal contained between these citation entries.  
3. Because the extraction rubric requires explicit identification of:
   • risks/problems  
   • mechanistic analyses and theoretical insights  
   • design rationales and implementation mechanisms  
   • validation evidence and proposed interventions  

   none of these elements can be recovered when only the titles, authors, and publication information of external works are present.  
4. Attempting to infer internal content of the referenced works (e.g. “The secret of our success” or “Adam: a method for stochastic optimisation”) would demand wholesale speculation about each source’s claims, evidence, and interventions—violating the requirement to base nodes and edges on the “closest preceding data source section titles.”  
5. Consequently, any network we might manufacture would be disconnected from the actual data source and would have evidence-confidence level 1 (speculative) across the board, defeating the purpose of a rigorous, mergeable knowledge fabric.

How to enable successful extraction in future iterations:
• Provide the main text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) or at least an extended abstract of a single study, report, or policy paper rather than only its reference list.  
• If the intention is to aggregate claims across a bibliography, supply short summaries or annotated notes for each citation that state the key risk addressed, the core finding, and any intervention recommended.  
• Alternatively, narrow the task to a single target work (e.g. Henrich 2015) and include the relevant paragraphs so that causal chains can be traced.

Because zero compliant nodes or edges can legitimately be extracted, no JSON fabric is returned.

Extraction-confidence score: 3 / 100 (essential information absent — failure expected under current input).
